For the full picture of how the WWDC announcements land for pass issuers, see our I/O 2026 and WWDC 2026 Wallet roundup.

## Who it is for

Pass Designer is for anyone who wants to see an Apple Wallet pass design before shipping it: developers replacing the edit-build-install loop, and designers producing a client-ready pass mockup that is pixel-identical to the real thing. Pass Builder is for teams that run their own server infrastructure, hold their own Apple certificate, and want the template-to-signed-pass step as a maintained package instead of homegrown signing code. [...] ## What Pass Designer does

Before Pass Designer, designing an Apple Wallet pass meant writing `pass.json` by hand against Apple’s documentation, bundling images at the right sizes, signing the bundle, and installing it on an iPhone to see whether the layout worked. The feedback loop ran through a build step every time a label moved. Apple’s own framing in the session: passes have gained a decade of features, and it has become hard to connect what the pass bundle describes to what renders on the device.

Pass Designer replaces that loop with a sidebar editor and a live preview that is true to iOS rendering, on both iPhone and Apple Watch. The sidebar covers every part of a pass template: [...] Pass Designer is a Mac app by Apple for designing Apple Wallet pass templates. Apple introduced it at WWDC 2026 in the “What’s new in Wallet” session (session 209) alongside iOS 27. It is Apple’s first first-party visual tool for making passes: a what-you-see-is-what-you-get editor that renders the pass exactly as iOS will, and saves the result as a `.pkpasstemplate` file that the companion Pass Builder package turns into signed, distributable passes.

The beta is available to download now with a free Apple Account; it requires macOS 27, which is itself in beta until the fall 2026 public release. We will update this page as the tools move out of beta.

results.title: Pass Designer for Apple Wallet: From Design to Distribution
results.content:
## What Apple’s Pass Designer changes

With Pass Designer, Apple introduces a visual way to build Wallet passes. You can create layouts, adjust colors and fields, and immediately see how the pass will appear on a device. The tool also helps validate your pass structure while you work, reducing errors early in the process.

This lowers the barrier to entry significantly and makes Wallet technology more accessible to designers and product teams.

At the same time, it’s important to understand that Pass Designer focuses on the creation of a pass itself. It helps you define how a pass looks and what information it contains, but it does not cover everything that is needed to use that pass in a real-world scenario.

# The Pass Designer Menu

Navigating the Pass Designer

Written by Paul Tomes

Table of contents

# Introduction

The Pass Designer is a powerful tool that enables users to create and customize digital passes for Apple and Google Wallet. Whether you're designing a loyalty card, event ticket, or membership pass, the Pass Designer simplifies the process with its intuitive interface and robust features. If you're new to the tool, taking the time to familiarize yourself with its various areas and functionalities will help you create professional, polished passes with ease. [...] [](

Important Note: If this is a live project and you’ve already issued passes, the updated design will be pushed to all passes in users’ wallets. If you want to test or preview your design changes before applying them to a live project, we recommend using a test project to avoid unintended updates to issued passes.

# Why Familiarize Yourself with the Pass Designer?

Understanding the Pass Designer’s interface and tools is essential for creating professional, high-quality digital passes. By mastering the Google Pass Designer, Apple Pass Designer, Enrolment Form Designer, Field Manager, Design Settings, and Pass Colour Editor, you’ll be equipped to design passes that are both functional and visually stunning. Don’t forget to save your work regularly to keep your progress secure! [...] If you’re in the Apple Wallet Pass Designer view, you’ll see options to customize the background color, label text color, and value text color for Apple Wallet.
 If you’re in the Google Wallet Pass Designer view, you’ll see options to customize the theme color for Google Wallet.

Note that the background color you select will be applied to both Apple and Google Wallet passes. This means Apple Wallet cannot have a different background color than Google Wallet. Use this tool to ensure your passes are visually consistent and aligned with your brand.
